churches.name: Cornerstone Chapel, an Apostolic Church

score_notes.christology: Oneness Apostolic theology rejects the Trinity — teaches Jesus-Only modalism (Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are not distinct persons but modes of one God = Jesus). This is a historic heresy (condemned at Nicaea/Constantinople).
score_notes.soteriology: Apostolic churches typically teach baptismal regeneration and speaking in tongues as necessary for salvation — 'Acts 2:38 salvation plan' that adds works to justification by faith alone.
score_notes.denomination: Apostolic/Oneness tradition stands outside Nicene orthodoxy; no accountability to historic trinitarian Christianity.
score_notes.mens: No men's ministry found.
score_notes.gender: Male lead pastor (Robert Eaby Jr.); Oneness Pentecostal tradition historically allows women in various ministry roles; no explicit patriarchal household or male-elder-only framework confirmed.

churches.assessment: Cornerstone Chapel is an Apostolic/Oneness Pentecostal church — and that's a hard stop for theological alignment. Oneness Pentecostalism denies the eternal distinction of the three persons of the Trinity (Father, Son, Holy Spirit), teaching instead that 'Jesus' is the only name of God and the three are merely different modes. This places it outside the bounds of Nicene orthodoxy — the same line historic Christianity drew in 325 AD. Additionally, most Apostolic churches teach that speaking in tongues and baptism in 'Jesus' name only' are necessary for salvation, adding works to justification. The congregation may be sincere and passionate, but the core theological framework disqualifies it for anyone committed to trinitarian Christianity and faith-alone soteriology. Not recommended.
churches.gender_detail: Male lead pastor; Apostolic tradition varies — women's ministry role unclear in Oneness Pentecostalism

churches.assessment: Hope Presbyterian is one of the strongest finds on this list. Pastor Jonathan Dennis holds an MDiv from Reformed Theological Seminary — one of the top conservative Reformed seminaries in the world — and has been in EPC ministry since 2010. The EPC is a conservative evangelical Presbyterian denomination that affirms inerrancy, salvation by faith alone, and Nicene orthodoxy. It sits to the right of mainline Presbyterians (PCUSA) but slightly more latitude than the PCA on women's ordination (letting local congregations set policy). With an RTS-trained lead pastor, the preaching quality and doctrinal grounding should be excellent. The church is mission-focused (Great Commission language throughout) and serves the broader FXBG/Spotsylvania/Stafford/King George area. A serious candidate for Moop's home church search.
churches.gender_detail: EPC allows congregational latitude on women's ordination; complementarian likely but unconfirmed at local level

churches.assessment: Fredericksburg UMC sits squarely in the post-split United Methodist Church — the branch that retained 'United Methodist' branding after the traditional/conservative wing departed to form the Global Methodist Church. The 2024 UMC General Conference removed all language restricting LGBTQ+ ordination and same-sex marriage. With a female senior pastor, multiple associate pastors, and UMC denominational accountability to a now-affirming hierarchy, this church does not align with Moop's theological convictions. The congregation may have sincere Christ-loving people in the pews, but the institutional framework is compromised.

churches.assessment: Calvary Chapel Fredericksburg checks most of the boxes Moop cares about. The Calvary Chapel movement is known above all for verse-by-verse expository Bible teaching — it's baked into the DNA (Chuck Smith legacy). The leadership page shows a clear elder/pastor structure with male pastoral leadership, a dedicated Men's Ministry leader (Joe Gallegos), and a full complement of ministries including youth, children, prayer, and outreach. CC churches typically hold to Scripture inerrancy, salvation by grace through faith alone, and complementarian leadership. The charismatic-adjacent culture (CC is Spirit-friendly but not charismatic in the more extreme sense) may be a moderate fit for Moop's background. The verse-by-verse preaching model is one of the best in evangelical Christianity. Strong candidate.
churches.gender_detail: Male-only pastoral leadership; Calvary Chapel maintains complementarian DNA with male elders and pastors

churches.assessment: Chancellor Baptist's doctrinal statement is genuinely solid — they affirm Scripture as God's Word, salvation through Christ alone, eternal security, baptism by immersion, Great Commission evangelism. The church's mission statement (pointing people to Christ and into His church) is clear and healthy. The honest concern is BGAV affiliation: unlike SBC, BGAV is the moderate Virginia Baptist stream that parted ways over inerrancy and women's ordination. That doesn't automatically mean Chancellor is progressive — many BGAV churches are theologically conservative at the local level — but the accountability structure is to a moderate denomination. Before joining, Moop should ask: Does Chancellor have an elder board? What is the stance on women in pastoral roles? Pastor Cameron West's background and convictions are unknown — worth a direct conversation.

Luke Taylor is a sincere pastor with solid theology on the essentials — Christ is the only way, the Bible is authoritative, gender is binary. score_notes.christology: Churches of Christ affirm Christ as the only Savior; Trinitarian orthodoxy affirmed.
score_notes.scripture: Churches of Christ hold a high view of Scripture as the sole rule of faith and practice — this is central to Restoration Movement identity. Their public statement: 'We plead for religious unity among all believers based on the Bible.'
score_notes.gender: Traditional Churches of Christ consistently hold male-only eldership with women not serving in teaching authority over men. This congregation follows the traditional CoC pattern. Green on gender specifically — soteriology is the concern, not gender roles.
score_notes.leadership: Elder-led structure is standard in Churches of Christ — a plurality of male elders is the norm, which is more accountable and biblical than single-pastor models.
score_notes.soteriology: Red flag: Churches of Christ historically teach baptismal regeneration — that water baptism (immersion) is necessary for salvation, not just a response to salvation. The classic formula is 'believe + repent + be baptized = receive Holy Spirit + forgiveness.' This adds a work to justification, which is incompatible with faith-alone soteriology.
score_notes.cultural: No DEI/progressive cultural language found; mission statement is straightforwardly Bible-centered.
score_notes.denomination: Self-described as non-denominational but part of the Churches of Christ tradition — a distinct stream with its own theological DNA (restoration, baptism, a cappella worship in most congregations).
score_notes.preaching: Churches of Christ are known for verse-by-verse Bible teaching; expository DNA is strong.
score_notes.mens: No dedicated men's ministry found.

churches.assessment: Fredericksburg Church of Christ has a lot going for it: high Scripture authority, Trinitarian orthodoxy, complementarian leadership with male elder plurality, expository DNA, and no cultural drift indicators. The congregation explicitly states they are 'not a denomination, but simply Christians that belong to the body of believers of which Christ is the head' — that's a healthy posture. The hard stop for a faith-alone evangelical like Moop: Churches of Christ traditionally teach that baptism is necessary for salvation, not merely a sign of it. This is the theological fault line that separates the Restoration Movement from mainstream evangelicalism — and it's a real one. Not a cult, not heresy in the broad sense, but incompatible with sola fide. Worth a conversation with leadership to clarify their exact position on baptism and salvation before getting deeper. Some congregations in this tradition have moved toward a more grace-emphasis soteriology; some have not.
churches.gender_detail: Male-only eldership and leadership (Churches of Christ tradition); no women in teaching authority over men

churches.assessment: Saint Mary's is a large, active Catholic parish in Fredericksburg under the conservative Diocese of Arlington. Fr. Mosimann serves as Vicar Forane — essentially the area dean — indicating a significant, well-resourced congregation. Trinitarian orthodoxy is rock-solid; male-only priesthood is firmly complementarian; accountability structure is hierarchical and thorough. From a Protestant evangelical standpoint, the theological divergence is real: Catholic soteriology adds sacraments, merit, and ecclesial mediation to faith; Scripture sits alongside Tradition rather than above it. These are not minor differences — they were the substance of the Reformation. That said, for a man interested in robust liturgy, deep historical tradition, strong pro-life stance, and conservative moral theology, the Diocese of Arlington Catholic experience is among the best available. Not the right fit for a faith-alone evangelical, but should be evaluated on its own terms.

churches.assessment: Shiloh Baptist Church (Old Site) is one of Fredericksburg's most historically significant congregations — founded in 1854 from a congregation dating to the early 1800s, serving the African American community through slavery, the Civil War, Reconstruction, and the Civil Rights era. Notable members include John Washington (whose escape from slavery inspired a Trail to Freedom) and Rev. Lawrence A. Davies (pastor and mayor of Fredericksburg). The church's commitment to community (free Wednesday breakfast with Micah Ecumenical Ministries, active youth ministry) reflects genuine love. The honest theological concern is the public framing: 'no barriers to God's grace, no walls of exclusion' and 'inclusive embrace' language combined with minimal gospel-clarity and strong social-service identity suggests the congregation may have drifted toward social gospel territory where the transforming work of Christ is framed primarily in terms of social healing rather than personal salvation and sanctification. This is a pattern in mainline-influenced progressive Baptist churches. Moop should visit and listen to the sermons directly before drawing conclusions.

churches.assessment: Research confirmed the Communion of Reformed Evangelical Churches (CREC) has no known church or mission plant in the Fredericksburg, Spotsylvania, or Stafford County area as of March 2026. The CREC church directory (crechurches.org) was reviewed and no Virginia entries near FXBG were found — the nearest CREC churches in Virginia are likely in the Richmond or Northern Virginia areas. For Moop's reference: CREC is a high-quality Reformed denomination — theologically conservative, confessional (Westminster Standards), complementarian, and expository — founded in 1998 and associated with names like Douglas Wilson, Peter Leithart, and James Jordan. One caveat: some CREC churches hold Federal Vision theological positions on baptism and covenant, which not all evangelicals affirm. If a CREC plant ever appears in FXBG, it would be worth serious investigation. For now, the PCA (New City Fellowship, Hope Presbyterian) and SBC options (Spotswood Baptist, Massaponax Baptist) are the strongest Reformed-adjacent options in the area.

churches.assessment: Zion Presbyterian Church is one of the most theologically rigorous options in the Fredericksburg area. It is a congregation of the Free Church of Scotland (Continuing) — a denomination that holds to Biblical inerrancy and the original Westminster Confession of Faith without modification. This is not the touchy-feely mainline PCUSA Presbyterian; this is hard-core Westminster Calvinist confessionalism. Pastor Rom Prakashpalan is a converted Hindu/atheist who came to faith through hearing the Gospel (Romans 10:17), graduated RPTS with an MDiv, and was installed here in November 2024. The church is very new (2023) and meets at Fredericksburg Christian School. Two Sunday services (10:30 AM and 2:00 PM) plus a Thursday prayer meeting demonstrate seriousness. The lack of men's ministry is understandable for a plant this young. For a man who wants unapologetic Reformed confessionalism and a pastor with a powerful conversion testimony, this is a must-visit.

churches.assessment: Fredericksburg Presbyterian Church on Princess Anne Street is a historic congregation with over 200 years of ministry in the city — that heritage is real and worth noting. However, it affiliates with the Presbyterian Church (USA), which formally departed from biblical authority in 2015 by voting to approve same-sex marriage, ordains women at all levels of church government, and does not affirm biblical inerrancy. The church's website language about 'preserving God's creation' and 'honoring gifts' suggests alignment with the denomination's progressive trajectory. For a man committed to complementarian Christianity, biblical inerrancy, and historic sexual ethics, PCUSA is a disqualifying affiliation. This entry serves as a reference so men visiting downtown Fredericksburg understand why this historic church, despite its beautiful building and heritage, is not the right choice theologically.
